text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.4% today as oil prices jumped sharply on geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Brent crude—the global oil benchmark—spiked more than 4% after reports that the U.S. is deploying a third aircraft-carrier strike group to the region, and the UK Prime Minister suggested Iran was involved in an incident at a British air base. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to higher revenue from selling oil.

The timing matters: the stock had fallen about 4.7% over the prior two weeks amid broader uncertainty, so today's bounce reflects a shift in near-term sentiment driven by this specific geopolitical event rather than a reversal of that downtrend.
